proposals.before: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi).
proposals.after: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.
proposals.reason: The parenthetical Sima Yi is not in the Chinese and invents a personal name the unit does not give.

proposals.before: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor named Sima Shi General Who Stabilizes the Army and regent in the combined office of Great General.
proposals.after: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor named Sima Shi General-in-Chief Who Comforts the Army to assist in government.
proposals.reason: 撫軍大將軍 is a single office, not two combined posts; 輔政 means assisting in government.

proposals.before: Sima Shi wept and said, "My forebears enjoyed extraordinary favor from the house of Wei; the late emperor, on his deathbed, bound us with his final charge.
proposals.after: Sima Shi wept and said, "Former ministers received generations of extraordinary favor; the late emperor, on his deathbed, entrusted them with a testamentary edict.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 先臣 is 'former ministers' (the speaker's official predecessors), not biological 'forebears'; 托以遣詔 is entrusting a testamentary edict.

proposals.before: Pure Music assistant Pang Xi’s pleas went unheeded.
proposals.after: When the Assistant Director of Pure Music Pang Xi remonstrated with the emperor, the emperor did not listen.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops both the remonstrance and the emperor as agent, which the Chinese 清商丞龐熙諫帝，帝弗聽 states explicitly.

proposals.before: Let him ascend to the position of Chancellor of State, increase fief by nine thousand, together with the previous forty thousand households;
proposals.after: Let him ascend to the position of Chancellor of State and increase the fief by nine thousand households, making forty thousand households together with what he already held;
proposals.reason: 並前四萬戶 means a combined total of 40,000 including prior holdings, not 9,000 plus a previous 40,000.

proposals.before: Down to King Cheng of Zhou, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao served as assistants; therefore they were able to depart from the classics and distinguish aims, secure the Way and rejoice in their tasks.
proposals.after: Down to King Cheng of Zhou, Dan and Wang served as assistants; therefore he could complete the classics and set his aims, rest in the Way, and take joy in his work.
proposals.reason: 離經辯志 is the Liji idiom for finishing the classics and determining one's orientation, not abandoning the classics; 旦望 are the two aides, and the abilities belong to the king they tutored.

proposals.before: The Son of Heaven, receiving the seal, was lazy; lifting his toes high; the Emperor heard and worried about it.
proposals.after: The Son of Heaven, on receiving the seal, grew slack and walked with a high step; the Emperor heard of it and worried.
proposals.reason: The source is a coordinated judgment of careless bearing (惰, 舉趾高), not two broken clauses about laziness.

proposals.before: Under King Cheng the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao stood at his side, so the heir could move beyond rote text, fix his purpose, find peace in the Way, and take joy in ruling.
proposals.after: Down to King Cheng, Dan and Wang served as aides, so he could finish the classics and set his aims, rest in the Way, and take joy in his work.
proposals.reason: Chinese 旦望 is Zhou Gong Dan and Tai Gong Wang (Lü Wang), not the Duke of Shao; 離經辯志 is completing the classics and fixing aims.

proposals.before: The commandant at Anfeng Ford ran him down, struck off his head, and sent it to Luoyang by post-horse.
proposals.after: The commandant at Anfeng Ford ran him down, struck off his head, and sent it to the capital by post-horse.
proposals.reason: Chinese 京都 means the capital; the idiomatic English invents Luoyang, which is not in this unit.

proposals.before: To give him the same posthumous wording as the two Wei founders fills me with dread.
proposals.after: To give him the same posthumous name as the two ancestors fills me with dread.
proposals.reason: Chinese 二祖 is 'two ancestors' and does not name Wei; the gloss 'Wei founders' is an interpretive addition.

proposals.before: Emperor Wen, personal name Zhao and courtesy name Zishang, was Sima Shi’s full younger brother.
proposals.after: Emperor Wen, personal name Zhao and courtesy name Zishang, was Sima Shi’s uterine younger brother.
proposals.reason: Chinese 母弟 specifies a younger brother by the same mother; idiomatic 'full younger brother' overstates the kinship as necessarily sharing both parents.

proposals.before: When the great army punished Wang Ling, the Emperor supervised Huainan north military affairs and led troops to assemble at Xiang.
proposals.after: When the great army punished Wang Ling, the Emperor supervised military affairs north of the Huai and led troops to assemble at Xiang.
proposals.reason: 淮北 is the region north of the Huai, not 'Huainan north'; the calque reverses the geography.

proposals.before: The two armies suffered rout; by sitting he lost the marquisate.
proposals.after: The two armies suffered rout; he was held responsible and lost the marquisate.
proposals.reason: 坐 here is legal implication for the defeat, not literal sitting.

proposals.before: Quan Yi’s mother was a daughter of Sun Quan; out of favor in Wu, she was escorted to the Wei lines by two nephews of Quan Duan.
proposals.after: Quan Yi’s mother was a daughter of Sun Quan; having given offense in Wu, Quan Duan’s elder brother’s sons Hui and Yi escorted her mother over in flight.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 禕 and 儀 and the kinship 全端兄子 are omitted from the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: Quan Jing was still in Shouchun with Zhuge Dan; Zhong Hui forged letters in the names of the defectors to bait him.
proposals.after: Yi’s elder brother Jing was then in Shouchun; using Zhong Hui’s plan, they forged letters in Hui’s and Yi’s names to deceive Jing.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English invents Zhuge Dan beside Jing; the Chinese only places 儀兄靜 at Shouchun and names 禕、儀 on the forged letters.

proposals.before: In the sixth month of summer, the fourth year, Jingzhou was split into two commands: Wang Ji took Xinye and Zhou Ta took Xiangyang.
proposals.after: In the sixth month of summer, the fourth year, Jingzhou was split into two commands: Wang Ji took Xinye and Zhou Tai took Xiangyang.
proposals.reason: 州泰 is the same officer earlier rendered Zhou Tai; Zhou Ta splits the name.

proposals.before: The Son of Heaven, because the Emperor for three generations was chief minister, government was not of himself issuing, inwardly could not be at peace, also feared deposition and humiliation, was about to ascend the gallery and summon the hundred officials and carry out dismissal.
proposals.after: The Son of Heaven, because the Emperor's house had been chief ministers for three generations, government was not issuing from himself, inwardly could not be at peace, also feared deposition and humiliation, was about to ascend the gallery and summon the hundred officials and carry out dismissal.
proposals.reason: 帝三世宰輔 means three generations of the Sima house as chief ministers, not that this one Emperor personally served three generations.

proposals.before: He sent his uncle Xun Yi in a litter to fetch Chen Tai into a side room and asked, "Xuanbo, what is the realm going to say of me now?"
proposals.after: He sent his maternal uncle Xun Yi in a litter to fetch Chen Tai into a side room and asked, "Xuanbo, what is the realm going to say of me now?"
proposals.reason: 舅 is specifically maternal uncle; the idiomatic rendering under-specifies the kinship.

proposals.before: Annoyed by Deng Ai’s foot-dragging, Sima Zhao made his chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng’s deputy to talk sense into him; Deng then accepted the order.
proposals.after: Annoyed by Deng Ai’s foot-dragging, Sima Zhao made his chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng Ai’s major to talk sense into him; Deng then accepted the order.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line fuses Shi Zuan with Deng and renders 司馬 as deputy; the Chinese appoints 師纂 as 艾司馬 (Deng Ai's major).

proposals.before: Yet you are quiet and respectful early and late, toiling and humble before dawn; although the Grandfather's assisting left and right civil and martial, Duke of Zhou's toil for the royal house—nothing is added beyond this.
proposals.after: Yet you are quiet and respectful early and late, toiling and humble before dawn; although Shangfu’s assisting left and right in civil and martial affairs, and the Duke of Zhou’s toil for the royal house—nothing is added beyond this.
proposals.reason: 尚父 is the honorific Shangfu, not ‘grandfather’; the literal line mistranslates the title used of the Zhou founding aide.

proposals.before: When Huan and Wen saved the house of Zhou, they too received the nine gifts, that their great merit might shine as a pattern for posterity.
proposals.after: In the crisis of Hui and Xiang, Huan and Wen by their labor of supporting the throne still received the rite of bestowed commands, all used to make former great virtue shine as a model for later ages.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 惠襄之難 (the hardship of Kings Hui and Xiang) and invents ‘nine gifts’ where the Chinese has 錫命之禮.

proposals.before: We send a credential bearer, concurrent Minister of Education and metropolitan commandant, to hand you seal, ribbon, patent, gold beast tallies one through five, and bamboo tallies one through ten.
proposals.after: We order Gai, Bearer of Credentials, concurrent Minister of Education and Metropolitan Commandant, to confer at once the seal and ribbon, the patent, gold beast tallies one through five, and bamboo envoy tallies one through ten.
proposals.reason: Chinese names the envoy 陔; the idiomatic English omits the personal name and treats 陔即 as if no named officer were present.

proposals.before: Order Bearer of Credentials, concurrently Minister of Education, Metropolitan Commandant immediately to confer seal-ribbon and patent text, gold beast tallies first through fifth, bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth.
proposals.after: Order Bearer of Credentials, concurrently Minister of Education, Metropolitan Commandant Gai to confer at once the seal-ribbon and patent text, gold beast tallies first through fifth, bamboo envoy tallies first through tenth.
proposals.reason: 陔 is the envoy’s given name; 即授 is ‘confer at once.’ The literal line reads 陔即 as ‘immediately’ and drops the person.

proposals.before: From your grandfather the chancellor onward, each generation has aided Wei with shining virtue until the court is clean of chaff and the people free of slander.
proposals.after: From the former Chancellor of State onward, each generation has aided Wei with shining virtue until the court is clean of chaff and the people free of slander.
proposals.reason: Chinese 先相國 names the former Chancellor of State, not a grandfather; the idiomatic kinship overstates the source.

proposals.before: On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir to the duchy of Jin.
proposals.after: On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir apparent of Jin.
proposals.reason: After the kingship grant in s0418, 晉世子 is the Jin heir apparent, not heir to a duchy.

decisions.reason: The focus unit names only 景皇帝, 師, 子元, and 宣帝. Its parenthetical “Sima Yi” is not in the source; removing that supplied name restores a literal translation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 景皇帝諱師，字子元，宣帝長子也。

decisions.after: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor appointed Sima Shi General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
decisions.reason: 撫軍大將軍 is one office and 輔政 means assisting in government. “General Who Pacifies the Army” avoids the proposed awkward office expansion while removing the invented combined post and regency.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 命帝以撫軍大將軍輔政

decisions.after: Sima Shi wept and said, "My late father received extraordinary favor through successive reigns; when the late emperor was dying, he entrusted him with a testamentary edict.
decisions.reason: Here 先臣 is Sima Shi’s deferential reference to his deceased father, not biological forebears or an unspecified plural of officials. The revised wording keeps the personal relation and the testamentary entrustment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 先臣受曆世殊遇，先帝臨崩，托以遣詔

decisions.reason: 清商丞龐熙諫帝，帝弗聽 explicitly records Pang Xi’s remonstrance and the emperor’s refusal to listen. The proposed wording restores both omitted actions.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 清商丞龐熙諫帝，帝弗聽

decisions.reason: 並前四萬戶 sets the combined fief at forty thousand households, including prior holdings. The prior literal wrongly reads it as nine thousand added to a pre-existing forty thousand.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 增邑九千，並前四萬戶

decisions.after: By the time of King Cheng of Zhou, Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang served as his aides; therefore he could complete the Classics and set his aims, rest in the Way, and take joy in his work.
decisions.reason: 旦望 are Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang, not the Duke of Shao; the king, not the two aides, is the subject of the resulting abilities. This wording also avoids overlapping the prior English title surfaces.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 逮至周成，旦望作輔，故能離經辯志，安道樂業

decisions.reason: 受璽惰，舉趾高 is a coordinated description of slack conduct and an arrogant gait. The proposal turns the broken literal clauses into that coherent judgment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 天子受璽惰，舉趾高

decisions.after: By the time of King Cheng of Zhou, Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang served as his aides, so he could complete the Classics and set his aims, rest in the Way, and take joy in his work.
decisions.reason: The idiomatic field also misidentifies 旦望 as the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao. The revision restores Duke Dan and Grand Duke Wang, keeps King Cheng as the subject, and avoids overlapping prior English title surfaces.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 逮至周成，旦望作輔，故能離經辯志，安道樂業

decisions.reason: 京都 says “the capital”; it does not identify Luoyang in this unit. The proposal removes the unsupported place-name while retaining the pursuit, beheading, and relay.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 傳首京都

decisions.reason: 二祖 means “the two ancestors.” The source does not specify Wei founders, so the proposal removes an interpretive historical gloss from the idiomatic field.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 今諡與二祖同

decisions.after: Emperor Wen, personal name Zhao and courtesy name Zishang, was Sima Shi’s younger brother by the same mother.
decisions.reason: 母弟 specifies a younger brother sharing the mother; “full younger brother” improperly asserts shared father as well. The revision states the supplied kinship plainly.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 景帝之母弟也

decisions.reason: 淮北 is the territory north of the Huai River, not “Huainan north.” The proposed literal corrects the geographical relation without changing the reported command.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 督淮北諸軍事

decisions.reason: 坐 is legal responsibility in this context: the military defeat caused loss of the marquisate. The proposal removes the nonsensical literal “by sitting.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 二軍敗績，坐失侯

decisions.after: Quan Yi’s mother was a daughter of Sun Quan. Having given offense in Wu, she fled over with Hui and Yi, sons of Quan Duan’s elder brother.
decisions.reason: The unit names Hui and Yi and identifies them as sons of Quan Duan’s elder brother. The revision preserves those names and kinship without the ambiguous “her mother” in the proposal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 全端兄子禕及儀奉其母來奔

decisions.reason: 儀兄靜 places Yi’s elder brother Jing at Shouchun; 用鐘會計 attributes the stratagem to Zhong Hui, and 作禕、儀書 names the forged identities. The proposal removes the invented Zhuge Dan.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 儀兄靜時在壽春，用鐘會計，作禕、儀書以譎靜

decisions.reason: 州泰 is the personal name Zhou Tai. The current idiomatic field truncates it to “Zhou Ta”; the proposed correction preserves the name consistently.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 州泰鎮襄陽

decisions.reason: 帝三世宰輔 refers to three generations of the Sima house holding chief-ministerial power, not one emperor serving as chief minister across three generations.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝三世宰輔，政非己出

decisions.reason: 舅 specifically denotes a maternal uncle. The proposed idiomatic translation makes that kinship explicit while preserving the rest of the scene.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣其舅荀顗

decisions.reason: 使主簿師纂為艾司馬 makes chief clerk Shi Zuan Deng Ai’s 司馬, a major; it does not fuse their names or appoint a generic deputy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 使主簿師纂為艾司馬以喻之

decisions.after: Yet you are calm and reverent from dawn to dusk, laboring humbly before daylight; even Shangfu’s support in civil and military affairs and the Duke of Zhou’s toil for the royal house did not surpass it.
decisions.reason: 尚父 is the honorific Shangfu, not a grandfather. The revision also repairs the comparative grammar of 罔以加焉 while retaining the two historical comparisons.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雖尚父之左右文武，周公之勤勞王家，罔以加焉

decisions.after: During the crises of Kings Hui and Xiang, Dukes Huan and Wen, for their work in protecting and supporting the throne, still received the rites of conferral; all this made the great virtue of earlier times shine as a model for later ages.
decisions.reason: 惠襄之難 and 錫命之禮 are both omitted or distorted by the current idiomatic field. The revision restores the crises and the rites of conferral without inventing the nine gifts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 惠襄之難，桓文以翼戴之勞，猶受錫命之禮，咸用光疇大德，作范於後

decisions.reason: 陔 is the named envoy, followed by 即授 (“confer at once”). The proposed idiomatic field restores Gai and accurately identifies the sequence of insignia.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 命使持節、兼司徒、司隸校尉陔即授印綬策書

decisions.reason: The same sequence identifies Gai as the envoy and 即授 as “confer at once.” The proposed literal fixes the prior parsing that dropped the person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 司隸校尉陔即授印綬策書

decisions.reason: 先相國 means the former Chancellor of State. It supplies no kinship term, so “your grandfather” is unsupported and the proposed correction is warranted.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自先相國以來

decisions.reason: 晉世子 is the heir apparent of Jin after the earlier elevation; it is not an heir to a duchy. The proposed wording gives the office correctly.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 命中撫軍新昌鄉侯炎為晉世子
